title: BackUp2.0: Pilot study of a digital intervention to promote subjective back health and physical activity in the daily working lives of people with and without chronic back pain
summary:
Low back pain affects a substantial proportion of the population. Recent research suggests that modifiable risk factors, such as low levels of physical activity and prolonged sitting, represent promising targets for interventions aimed at preventing and treating chronic low back pain. Guided by the Intervention Mapping Approach, an interdisciplinary team of psychologists, biomechanics, physiotherapists, and psychotherapists develop and evaluate the mobile health intervention “BackUp2.0”.  The intervention is designed to support individuals to incorporate more exercise breaks for the back (i.e. targeted back exercises) into their daily lives, particularly after prolonged periods of sitting.

Participants are equipped with accelerometers and a smartphone app. This allows for the very precise monitoring of patterns relating to periods of sedentary time, back health, pain, and associated psychosocial resources and risk factors in individuals’ natural environment. Participants undergo a spinal assessment, receive individualised training tailored to their needs, and are offered psychological counselling to support behaviour change. Over a subsequent period of approximately two months, participants then receive different forms of support features on different days. Based on the principle of real-time interventions (so-called Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions, JITAI), high-resolution daily measurements of physical activity enable, for example, the adaptation of interventions to current patterns of physical activity and sitting behaviour.

To gain a better understanding of individual trajectories, both people without chronic pain and those with chronic low back pain are studied over a period of 68 days using so-called n-of-1 studies (n=10 participants). Individual patterns of sitting and physical activity during work and leisure time, as well as self-reported pain and back health, are analysed alongside theoretically derived psychosocial factors (e.g., emotions, motivation).

In addition to individual effects of the intervention, the study aims to identify which factors – for each individual – are relevant to the engagement in back exercises, pain perception and back health. Furthermore, the feasibility and acceptability of BackUp2.0 will be examined.

The findings of this series of case studies are intended to serve as a basis for the development of tailored interventions aimed at reducing and preventing low back pain.

interventions.name:
The study consists of a series of micro-randomised single-case studies (n-of-1 studies). Each single-case study comprises two assessment phases. Two groups of participants will be included; the inclusion criteria are chronic low back pain or the absence of chronic pain (regardless of location).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Work involving a predominantly seated position (e.g. office work)
• No chronic pain or chronic low back pain (lasting > 12 weeks)
• Sufficient knowledge of German and the ability to understand and work through the questionnaires and instruction materials
Exclusion criteria:
• Working less than part-time
• Chronic pain in any part of the body, except for low back pain
• Participation in professional, competitive or elite sport
• Current participation in another study
• Acute infection
• Current pregnancy
• BMI > 29.444
• Postural problems/abnormalities of the lower limbs
• Recently operated hip
• Tumours, bone metastases
• Sensory impairments or neurological disorders
• Osteoporosis
• Spinal fracture
• Inflammation of the spine
• Prior spinal surgery
• Potent drug therapy (opioids, antiepileptics, muscle relaxants)
